description: How each kind of GTA thing near the car becomes something solid in BeamNG. One row per obstacle class; the id is sent in walls.hits.kind. Each row generates one entry of the obstacle table on both sides (gta/src/gen/obstacles.hpp, beamng gen/obstacles.lua).

columns.id: Class id (integer, sent on the wire)
columns.name: Class name
columns.bng_kind: slab (static box), post (static box sized from the prop), proxy_vehicle (solid moving proxy), none
columns.width: Box size along the surface, m (slab/post) or from GTA (proxy)
columns.thickness: Box size into the surface, m
columns.lifetime_ms: Removed when not seen again for this long

rows.name: ground
rows.notes: One slab per grid cell, top face through the cell's four corner heights (best-fit plane).

rows.name: wall
rows.source: horizontal probe hit with no entity (map collision: buildings, walls, barriers, trees)

rows.name: prop
rows.source: horizontal probe hit on an object entity wider than settings.prop_min_size (bollards, concrete blocks, dumpsters)
rows.notes: width/thickness come from the prop's model size (hits.size). Thinner props (lamp posts, signs, hydrants) break off in GTA, so they are not mirrored.

rows.name: ped
rows.source: none: GTA handles pedestrians hitting the proxy car
